exposed_dft_features.name: PCI BIST capability
exposed_dft_features.purpose: PCI Configuration Space offset 0Fh — Stat BIST set to 1 invokes vendor BIST; Completion Code reports pass/fail. Optional per AHCI 1.3.1 §2.1.9.

exposed_dft_features.name: SATA BIST FIS (FIS Type 0x58)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Software-built BIST Activate FIS — places the SATA link / device into a vendor-defined loopback / test mode. Command Header B bit indicates a BIST command.

exposed_dft_features.name: Activity LED + PxCMD.CCS
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Visual + register-level observability of which command slot is currently being serviced.

exposed_dft_features.name: PxSERR (SCR1)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Accumulates Link / PHY / Transport errors across multiple events — every CRC / Handshake / Internal / DataIntegrity / 10b-Decode / Disparity / COMWAKE / PhyInternal / PhyRdy-Change / Unknown-FIS event leaves a sticky bit.

exposed_dft_features.name: PxIS (per-port interrupt status)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Latches every completion / error event; software can replay the sequence of events by examining the bit pattern.

exposed_dft_features.name: Received FIS Structure (system memory)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Software can dump DSFIS / PSFIS / RFIS / SDBFIS / UFIS to reconstruct the most recent FIS of each type.

exposed_dft_features.name: Phy Event Counters (SATA 2.6)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Out of AHCI scope but visible to software via vendor SMART data — counts CRC errors, hardware-resets, R_ERR responses, recovery events; useful for field-failure triage.

fields.no_jtag_on_connector: There is no JTAG / scan port on the SATA connector. The SATA wire is a high-speed 4-pin differential link only.
fields.scan_chain_topology: AHCI does not define a scan-chain topology. Vendor HBA silicon ships with standard ATPG full / partial scan chains accessed at wafer / package probe.
bist_engines_in_hba: PCI Configuration Space BIST (optional, vendor-specific test patterns).
Vendor PHY BIST: line-rate pattern generators / checkers (PRBS / clock-pattern / packet-loopback) controllable via vendor PHY config registers.
fields.notes: AHCI's external observability is entirely register-level: PxSERR + PxIS + Received FIS Structure + PxTFD + PxSACT + PxCI capture enough state for software post-mortem. The BIST FIS path lets software invoke device-side loopback for cable / connector characterization. Internal HBA silicon DFT (scan, MBIST, IDDQ) is vendor-specific.
